memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But those who died in the plague numbered 24,000. - Num 25:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This single verse records a staggering loss: twenty-four thousand people died in the plague. We should not rush past this number. Behind it lie thousands of families, thousands of lives cut short because of the sin that swept through the camp. It is a sobering testimony to the deadly cost of turning from God.

Scripture does not soften this figure or explain it away, and neither should we. Sin has consequences, and they are often far more devastating than we imagine. What may have seemed to the men of Israel like a moment of pleasure with the Moabite women unleashed a catastrophe upon the whole nation. Sin never affects only the one who commits it.

This is meant to shake us out of our casual attitude toward sin. We so easily treat it as harmless, as a private matter of no great consequence. But sin is a killer. It brings death, spreads its poison, and leaves devastation in its wake. God records these numbers so that we will take sin seriously.

Yet against this dark backdrop, the gospel shines all the brighter. Where sin brought death to thousands, Christ brings life to all who trust in Him. He bore the deadly wages of sin in His own body so that we might live (1 Pet 2:24). Let the cost of sin drive you not to despair but to the Saviour who conquered death.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you grasp how costly and destructive sin truly is?
2. How does the death caused by sin heighten your gratitude for Christ's life?
3. Where are you tempted to treat sin as harmless?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me see sin for the killer it truly is, never treating it as harmless. Thank You that Christ bore its deadly cost so that I might have life in Him. Amen.
